title: Sextortion “help” firm took $60 million from victims, FTC alleges
content_md: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has filed a complaint accusing Digital Forensics Corporation of exploiting people already targeted by sextortionists . We have talked about sextortion and recovery scams in the past, but we never looked specifically at the combination. Apparently, there is a lot of money to be made for those ruthless enough to take money from victims already in a state of panic. The FTC has accused Digital Forensics Corporation, its owner Dmitry Belkin, and affiliated companies of misleading sextortion victims into paying at least $60 million for assistance that, in numerous instances, they did not provide. A federal court has temporarily halted the defendants’ activities while the case proceeds. Most of the time, sextortion emails are a bluff sent to a large number of targets to see if one takes the bait. But sextortion can also involve intimate images that someone really possesses. In those cases, a criminal threatens to share the material unless the victim pays, sends more images, or complies with other demands.
